quests.title: First Steps in Undeath
quests.description:
On your feet. Good - that's the hard part done and most of them take longer over it.

Overseer Krell. I'm the one who decides what becomes of you now that you've stopped being a corpse and started being a problem. Before you ask the questions they all ask: yes, you were dead. Yes, you're still dead. No, I can't tell you your name, and the ones who go looking for it first tend not to last the week.

Here's what matters today. The body answers now - it just doesn't answer the way it used to, and you'll not find that out standing in a graveyard being thoughtful about it.

There are duskbats in the treeline. They're about as gentle a thing as this valley offers. Go and find out what you've got.
quests.accept_text: The treeline, past the last of the graves. Find out what the body still does.
quests.turn_in_text:
Still standing. Still got both arms.

That's the whole of today's lesson and you'd be surprised how many don't manage it. Right - next thing.

quests.title: Stolen Supplies
quests.description:
Now something that'll teach you more about the Forsaken than killing bats will.

The village stores are shrinking. Nobody here eats - that's the joke, and I've heard it, and it isn't the point. Salt tins, rope, bandages, lamp oil. Things that keep a settlement standing rather than things that keep a person fed.

The ragged scavengers out past the fence have been dragging it off, and they take whatever glints without the faintest idea what any of it does.

I want all of it back. Every piece. The Dark Lady's bookkeeping is meticulous and so is mine, and that is not a small thing to learn on your first day: we are not animals picking over a ruin. We keep accounts.
quests.accept_text: The scavengers past the fence. Every piece - I'll know what's missing.
quests.turn_in_text:
[He checks it against a list, item by item, and ticks each one.]

All of it. Good.

That list is why there's a Deathknell at all. Remember that when somebody tells you we're just corpses that got lucky.

quests.title: Strays at the Gate
quests.description:
The dogs and the rats came to the graveyard for the obvious reason. That's nothing new - they've always come, and we've always let them, because what's in the ground is past caring.

Something in that soil has turned them. The strays are sick in a way I haven't got a word for, and they've started tearing at the gravediggers - and at the newly risen, which is what makes this yours.

You'll meet people out there who woke up this week and can't yet work out which way is the village. They cannot defend themselves. A fortnight ago neither could you.

Thin the strays, and the rats with them - the rats carry it into the stores, which makes it everyone's.
quests.accept_text: Round the graves and the gate. Mind the newly risen - they can't defend themselves.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's the yard safe for the ones still coming up.

You'll see a few of them wandering. Leave them be. They find their way or they don't, and standing over them helping doesn't change which.

quests.title: The Overrun Claim
quests.description:
North-west of here there's an old goldmine. It was a decent little operation - Gresk ran it, still runs it after a fashion, and the Undercity liked having it on the books.

Then the spiders came, and now the claim is web and bone and a foreman who has not left his own shaft in weeks.

The remarkable thing is that Gresk is still there at all. I'd have written him off and so would you, and he's still standing in the middle of it being extremely rude about his crew's work rate.

Clear the spiders off the claim so the man can breathe. Then talk to him - he'll have his own list, and his list is usually worth hearing.
quests.accept_text: The goldmine claim, north-west. Clear the spiders, then talk to Gresk.
quests.turn_in_text:
He's alive. Still standing in his own shaft complaining.

Good. Deathknell needs that mine and frankly Deathknell needs Gresk, though I'd thank you not to tell him I said the second part.

quests.title: Into the Hollow
quests.description:
Here's the thing about those spiders that Gresk hasn't worked out and I have.

They aren't wandering in. There are too many and they come too steadily, and a wandering population thins when you cull it. That one doesn't.

There's a cave beside the claim - Night Web's Hollow - and it is pouring them out like a spring.

Before anybody commits to going in there, I want eyes on the inner strand. Not a guess. Somebody who has stood in it and come back out.

And I'll be honest about my reasons: somebody in the Undercity will eventually ask me what is in that cave, and I intend to have an answer ready rather than a theory.

objectives.label: the inner strand of Night Web's Hollow

quests.accept_text: Night Web's Hollow, beside the claim. Get to the inner strand and come back out.
quests.turn_in_text:
A brood chamber. That deep in.

Right. Now I have an answer instead of a theory, and the answer is worse than the theory was, which is generally how this works.

quests.title: Broodmother Nesh'ka
quests.description:
Then we finish it, because a spring doesn't stop running on its own.

Nesh'ka sits at the centre of the Hollow, wrapped in her own silk. Every spider that claim has ever seen came out of her, and while she's down there the cave will keep filling this valley whatever we do at the top end.

Her brood will come at you before she does. That's not a tactic, that's just what a brood is for.

I don't need her negotiated with and I don't need the cave surveyed again. I need a corpse, and I need a handful of the brood brought back so the report has something in it besides my word.
quests.accept_text: The centre of the Hollow. The brood comes first - they always do.
quests.turn_in_text:
[Krell looks at what you've put on the table rather than at you.]

That's the claim saved and that's the valley quiet.

You've been dead about a month. I've had Deathguards take a year to be worth this much trouble.

quests.title: Word for Brill
quests.description:
Right. The valley's quiet for the first time since you were sewn together, and that means I'm finished with you.

Don't look like that. This is the good outcome. The ones I keep are the ones I can't send anywhere.

Take the road east. It leaves Deathknell for the Tirisfal Glades, and if you follow it through to the portal at the glade's heart it'll put you down at Brill - a real town, with a gate and a garrison and people who've been dead long enough to have opinions about it.

This note is for Deathguard Rennick at the gate. It says: 'Take this one, they bite.'

I'm not sorry. It's the best reference I've written in two years.
quests.accept_text: East out of the valley, through the glades to the portal, then on to Brill.
quests.turn_in_text:
[Rennick reads the note, snorts, and puts it in his coat.]

Krell doesn't write references. Krell writes complaints with names in them.

So you'll be useful. Welcome to Brill - stand over there and try not to look newly risen, it upsets the carters.

quests.title: Restless in the Ground
quests.description:
You can hear it too, can't you. From underneath. The scratching.

I don't know my name. I've been told that's normal and that it comes back for some of us, and I've noticed the people who say that don't look at me while they say it.

But I know that sound. It's the only thing I'm certain of in the whole world: that's what it sounds like from the inside, and I made it, and somebody heard me or I'd still be down there.

The grave-dwellers come up out of the mass pit and wander the field. They're not coherent - they're where I was a fortnight ago and some of them won't come further.

Put them back. Gently, if there's a gentle way. I'd want someone to have done it for me if I hadn't come up right.
quests.accept_text: The field by the mass pit. They've just come up. Gently, if you can.
quests.turn_in_text:
Thank you.

I stood out there afterwards and listened and there was nothing underneath at all. That's the first quiet I've had since I opened my eyes.

quests.title: Names on the Stones
quests.description:
A grave marker is supposed to be a name. That's its whole job - one piece of wood that says somebody was here and this is what they were called.

Up here they're mostly splinters, and the restless keep pulling them out of the ground and carrying them off. I've watched them do it. They hold them up. I think they're trying to read them, and I think most of them can't any more.

I want them collected. All the ones you can find.

[A pause.]

I know what I'm hoping for and I know how unlikely it is. But somebody wrote my name on a piece of wood once and hammered it into this hill, and if it's still out there in a dead man's hands I'd like it back.
quests.accept_text: Out in the grave field. The restless carry them off - gather what you can find.
quests.turn_in_text:
[She goes through them one at a time, slowly, turning each to the light.]

Not this one. Not this one either.

...No. None of them.

That's all right. I'll keep them anyway - they're somebody's. I'll stand them back up along the fence where they can be read, and whoever comes up next can look.

quests.title: The Gaunt Alpha
quests.description:
There's a stray out there that isn't like the others, and I need to ask you for something I can't ask the Overseer for.

He's grey and he's gaunt and he's twice the size of the rest, and he leads them through the graves at night. The villagers call him Mawgrin.

I call him the one who sits on my grave.

He does. Every night, on the open pit where I came up, and he sits there and he waits - and I cannot tell you whether he's waiting for me to go back down or for someone else to come up, and I have lain awake deciding which of those is worse.

Some of the pack will be with him. Please.
quests.accept_text: In the grave field after dark. He sits on the open pit - you'll know it.
quests.turn_in_text:
[She has been standing at the pit edge.]

It's empty. Just a hole in the ground with nothing sitting on it.

I'm going to have it filled in tomorrow. Properly, with a marker, and I'll put a name on it even if it has to be one I choose myself.

That's allowed, isn't it. Choosing one.

quests.title: Drill: Bones
quests.description:
You. Come here and pick that up. No - like that. Both hands until you know better.

I'm the Instructor, and my view is that a Forsaken learns by hitting things that are already dead, because the alternative is learning on things that aren't and I have buried enough students that way.

The Shadow Grave to the south is full of rattlecage skeletons. Crypt-dwellers, dead a very long time, extremely bad-tempered about the fact.

They are the finest sparring partner this valley offers. They never complain, they never tire, and they never stay down, which means you can be wrong four times and still walk back up that hill.

Go and be wrong four times.
quests.accept_text: The Shadow Grave, south. Be wrong as often as you need to - they don't stay down.
quests.turn_in_text:
Better. Still slow on the turn and you drop your guard when you step back, which will kill you eventually.

But better. Come back tomorrow and I'll find you something that hits harder.

quests.title: Wights of Shadow Grave
quests.description:
Now something that will teach you a distinction nobody in the village will explain properly, because they find it uncomfortable.

Wights. They are dead and they walk, and that is where the resemblance to us ends.

We were given will. That's the Dark Lady's gift and whatever anyone thinks of her, that is the thing she gave - you woke up and you were SOMEBODY, however little of him you can remember. A wight got none of that. There is nothing in there making decisions. There's hunger wearing a shape.

They're among the old stones of the Shadow Grave and they're drifting up toward the village.

Put them down. And look at one properly while you do, because half of being Forsaken is knowing exactly what you are not.
quests.accept_text: Among the old stones in the Shadow Grave. Look at one properly while you're there.
quests.turn_in_text:
And?

[He waits for your answer and nods at it.]

Good. Most of them say 'nothing behind the eyes' and most of them say it too quickly. You took your time.

That distinction is going to matter to you more than anything else I teach you.

quests.title: The Unburied
quests.description:
There's one in the Shadow Grave who's a lesson rather than a drill, so listen before you go down there swinging.

Ossric was the sexton. Before any of this, he buried half this village with his own hands - properly, with the rites, in the right order.

Nobody buried HIM. When it came round to his turn there was nobody left who did that work, and he went into the ground wrong or not at all.

He rises every night with the spade still in his hand and he goes looking for the grave that was never dug for him. He's been at it for years. He is extremely good at digging and he has never once found it.

So dig it. That's the whole task, and I'd like you to understand it as a kindness rather than a cull.
quests.accept_text: The Shadow Grave, with the spade. Understand it as a kindness, not a cull.
quests.turn_in_text:
You put him in it yourself. Good.

That's the lesson, and it's the last one I'll give you plainly: you'll spend a long time now among things that can't stop. Some of them need killing. Some of them need finishing. Learning to tell which is the entire art.

quests.title: Shrouds for the Unburied
quests.description:
Sexton Marrow. Mind the trench - that one's spoken for.

I'll tell you my standard and then you'll understand the request. In thirty years at this yard I have never left anybody uncovered. Not one. Plague, Scourge, the lot - whatever else went wrong up here, everyone who came through my hands went into the ground with linen over their face.

The zombies and the skeletons in the crypt-yard are wearing it. My linen. The good stuff, off bodies I wrapped myself, and they've torn it into scraps for no purpose whatsoever.

Get it back for me. I've a burial on Thursday and I would be ashamed to use anything less, and 'ashamed' is a strong word for a man in my condition to still have use for.
quests.accept_text: Off the zombies and skeletons in the crypt-yard. It's my linen - I'll know it.
quests.turn_in_text:
[He folds each scrap along its original crease without thinking about it.]

That's enough for Thursday and a little over.

Thirty years. Not one uncovered. I intend to keep saying that until there's nobody left to say it to.

quests.title: Dead Men Don't Dig
quests.description:
You're the one Krell sent. Right - don't touch the props, half of them are holding up the other half.

Gresk. Foreman, this claim, and before you make the obvious joke: yes, my crew was undead before the spiders came. That's why it was a good operation. They don't tire, they don't drink, and they don't go home.

The trouble is they also don't stop. I gave up supervising when the webs came down and they just... kept going. Still swinging, still working the face, and now they take a pick to anybody who comes near the shaft - including me, which I'd call ungrateful.

I can't reason with them. I've tried, at length, in a voice I'm not proud of. Try something else.
quests.accept_text: At the shaft face. They haven't stopped working - and they swing at anyone who nears it.
quests.turn_in_text:
Shaft's quiet.

[He stands in the entrance a while.]

They were a good crew. Best I ever had, and I include the breathing ones. Right - don't stand about, there's more wrong with this claim than diggers.

quests.title: Gold on a Thread
quests.description:
Here's a thing nobody believes until they've seen it, so don't argue, just go and look.

Those spiders weave with gold.

Not gold-coloured. GOLD. They've been through the old veins where the face was opened and they're lacing dust through the silk, and in the dark you can see the lines glinting across the whole chamber like somebody's strung a ballroom.

I've no idea why. I've a theory it's not deliberate and it just sticks to them, which would make it the only stupid thing anything in that cave does.

I want every strand. The Dark Lady likes gold, I like being a foreman the Dark Lady is pleased with, and those two facts are the entire structure of my career.
quests.accept_text: Through the web in the old workings. You'll see it glint - you can't miss it.
quests.turn_in_text:
[Gresk weighs a handful on a scale that has seen better decades.]

That's a month's output off a seam we'd written off, pulled out of a spider's web by a man who's been dead a fortnight.

I'm going to put that in the return exactly as it happened and let the Undercity make of it what they like.

quests.title: Goldfang
quests.description:
There's one down there that's been eating better than the rest.

The crew called it Goldfang, before the crew stopped talking. It's grown fat on whatever's in that seam and it's gone BRIGHT with it - the fangs have come up yellow and they catch the lamplight, which is the only warning you'll get in those tunnels.

It hunts the old workings. My workings. The ones with my crew's marks still chalked on the walls.

Some of the claim spiders run with it. Take those off it first.

And I'll be straight: I want it dead because it's in my tunnels, and I want the fangs because they'll fetch a price. Both reasons are real and I'm not going to pretend only the first one is.
quests.accept_text: The old workings, where the crew's chalk marks are. The fangs catch the light.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's my tunnels back.

Take a cut of the fangs. Don't argue - a foreman who doesn't pay his crew is a foreman with no crew, and at the moment you're the crew.

quests.title: Clearing the Hatchery
quests.description:
Last job on this claim, and it's the one that actually finishes it.

North-west corner of the Hollow there's a hatchery. Clutches hanging in the silk, rows of them, and a warden called Skrix minding the lot.

And on the far side there's the Pale Weaver, which I'd rather you heard about from me than met cold. It doesn't kill what it catches. It spins cocoons around the dead - already dead, understand, it goes and FETCHES them - and nobody including me has a satisfactory explanation for why.

Skrix, the Weaver, and the clutches. All of it, in one go. Leave any of the three and we'll be doing this again by spring.
quests.accept_text: The north-west chamber. Skrix, the Pale Weaver, and the clutches - all three.
quests.turn_in_text:
[He takes the lamp down into the Hollow himself, which he has not done since the webs came.]

Empty. Whole chamber, empty.

That's the claim. That's genuinely the claim, back on the books and working. Krell's going to be insufferable about it and he'll have earned it.

quests.title: Waters Gone Wrong
quests.description:
Sit, if you like. People don't, usually. They see where I'm sitting and they find somewhere to be.

This pond was a mourners' spot. That's what it was FOR - you came down here and sat on the bank and said whatever you needed to say to whoever you'd lost, and the water did the listening.

Now the dead talk back. The drowned come up out of the silt, and they moan, and they take hold of anybody near the bank.

I come anyway. Every day. I'd like you to understand that I'm not being brave about it - I simply have nowhere else to sit that's any better.

But I'd like it quiet while I'm here. That's all. Just quiet, for an hour.
quests.accept_text: Along the bank and in the shallows. She only wants it quiet for an hour.
quests.turn_in_text:
[She has not moved from the bank.]

Thank you. I sat the whole afternoon and nothing came up at all.

I said what I came to say, and the water did the listening, and that's the first time it's worked since I got here.

quests.title: Keepsakes in the Silt
quests.description:
I lost more than a husband to this water, though he's the one I came for.

Everybody who mourned here left something. That was the custom - you put a token on the bank when you'd finished saying your piece. Rings. Lockets. Ribbon, mostly, from the ones who had nothing else.

The pond-dead have collected them. All of them. I've seen them go along the bank picking the tokens up, and I cannot decide whether that's theft or whether something down there is HOARDING grief, which is a worse thought and the one I keep returning to.

Bring them back up. I'll find the families where there are families. Where there aren't, I'll keep them, and that's better than the silt.
quests.accept_text: The pond-dead have gathered them off the bank. Bring back what you can.
quests.turn_in_text:
[She lays them out on her skirt and touches each one.]

I know this ribbon. Girl from the mill - she came down three days running and never said a word, just sat and left it.

I'll keep them in the box with mine. Somebody ought to know they were left, even if it's only me.

quests.title: Quiet the Weeping
quests.description:
There's one voice out there louder than the others and I've been listening to it since the day I arrived.

They call it the Mourning Wren. It stands on the water at night - ON it - and it weeps, and every other dead thing in that pond takes up the sound and follows it.

The shades go to her. That's the part people miss. She isn't the loudest of them, she's the one they're all answering.

[A pause.]

I think I know who she is. I'm not going to say it out loud, and I'd be grateful if you didn't ask me afterwards whether I was right.

She's been weeping for years. Let her stop.
quests.accept_text: On the water at night. The shades follow her voice - take them first.
quests.turn_in_text:
[Isolde listens for a long time before she speaks.]

It's quiet.

You don't have to tell me anything. I'd rather you didn't. I'll sit here tomorrow and the day after and I'll know what I know, and that's mine.

Thank you. Genuinely.

quests.title: Scarecrows That Walk
quests.description:
Careful of the furrows, they're deeper than they look. I keep meaning to even them out and then I remember there's no reason to.

Orrel. I tended these fields before the fire and I tend them now, in my own fashion, which I'm aware is not farming.

The scarecrows I built are walking. They've come down off the frames and they go up and down the rows flailing at anything that moves, which is - and I want to be fair about this - exactly what I built them to do. I just built them rather better than I meant to, back when I had a reason to be good at it.

So it's my fault. I'd be grateful if you'd correct it, since I can't bring myself to take a hook to my own work.
quests.accept_text: Out in the furrows. They do exactly what I built them to do - that's the trouble.
quests.turn_in_text:
Thank you. I'll put the frames back up tomorrow with nothing on them.

A field wants scarecrows. It'll look wrong without, and looking right is about the only thing left I can do for it.

quests.title: Seeds Worth Saving
quests.description:
The fire took the house and it took the harvest and it took the gaffer, near enough.

It did not take the seed.

I'd buried the packets in the cellar - that's where seed goes, cool and dark, and it's the one bit of sense anybody on this farm ever credited me with. They came through it fine.

Now the burned hands are digging them up. They go down into the cellar and they come up with the packets and they carry them about the rows, and I think - I honestly think - they remember what seed is for.

Get them back for me. Nothing grows in Tirisfal. I'm not confused about that. I intend to try anyway, and I'd like the trying to be done properly with the real seed.
quests.accept_text: The burned farmhands carry them up out of the cellar. Get them back.
quests.turn_in_text:
[He checks each packet is still sealed before he puts it in his coat.]

All dry. Dry's everything with seed.

I'll put a row in along the south edge where the fire didn't reach the soil. If it comes to nothing I'll have had something to do all spring, and that's not nothing either.

quests.title: Old Gaffer Thorne
quests.description:
There's the gaffer, and I've left him till last because I'm a coward about it.

Thorne owned this farm. When the fire came he stayed to save the barn - sent everyone else down the road and stayed - and when the barn went he stayed anyway, and that's the whole of what happened to him.

He walks the burned rows now with a rusted scythe, cutting down whatever he finds. He thinks it's harvest. You can watch him do it and see the rhythm of it, the proper swing, the step between.

He took me on when nobody else would and he never once asked why I'd been let go elsewhere.

I owe him a decent burial. I cannot be the one who does it. Some of the hands will be with him.
quests.accept_text: Out in the burned rows with the scythe. Some of the hands will be with him.
quests.turn_in_text:
[Orrel has already dug it, at the top of the south edge, by hand.]

I got it ready this morning. Before I knew. I'd had it in mind for a year.

I'll say the words myself. That bit I can manage - it was only the other bit I couldn't.

quests.title: Eyes on the Crusade
quests.description:
Down. Behind the rock - there, and don't let the light catch you.

Verrick. I've been on these rocks a week watching the Scarlet Crusade build a camp outside our crypt.

Pickets on the line and torchbearers behind them, and a quantity of righteous noise that carries right across this valley at night. They sing. I want you to know that before you go down there, because it's unsettling in a way the fighting isn't.

I've watched long enough to be certain of one thing: they are not leaving on their own. This isn't a patrol that wandered in. They're digging in.

So we start thinning. Pickets and torchbearers both.
quests.accept_text: The picket line outside the crypt. Pickets and torchbearers both.
quests.turn_in_text:
Line's thinner and they've pulled the torches in closer.

That tells me more than the kill count does. A camp that tightens up is a camp that's started worrying about the dark.

quests.title: Burning Orders
quests.description:
The Scarlets write everything down. Everything.

Dispatches, sermons, duty rosters, orders for the next day's burning - all of it on paper, carried on the man, because they've decided that writing a thing down makes it righteous.

I'd call it a weakness if I could stop admiring the discipline of it.

Get me the dispatches off the pickets and the torchbearers. They keep them stuffed in their belts.

A dispatch in my hand tells me what the Crusade intends. What the Crusade intends tells me what to plan against. That is the entire business of scouting and everybody forgets it in favour of counting tents.
quests.accept_text: Stuffed in the belts of the pickets and torchbearers.
quests.turn_in_text:
[He reads them in order of date, which takes a while.]

They're not here for the valley.

They're here for the CRYPT, and they were here for the crypt before we ever noticed them. Everything outside is a screen for what's going on under it.

quests.title: Sergeant Halbrook
quests.description:
The sergeant on that line is the reason it holds.

Halbrook. Eight years of service and he has NAMED HIS HALBERD, which I mention not as a joke but because it tells you precisely what sort of man you're walking at.

He's certain. Not angry - certain, all the way down, that what we are is a sin and that cleaning it off this valley is simple work that simply has to be done. I've listened to him talk his pickets through it at the change of watch and he never raises his voice.

I've had him marked longer than anything else in this camp.

His pickets will come in around him. Take those first. The forecourt loses its sergeant, the line loses its spine.
quests.accept_text: On the picket line at the forecourt. His pickets will close in around him.
quests.turn_in_text:
Line's gone to pieces. They're standing in threes and looking at the crypt door instead of the valley.

That's what one man was worth. I'd like that noted, because when we write these up we always credit the numbers.

quests.title: Into the Scarlet Crypt
quests.description:
Now the crypt itself, and I'll tell you honestly where my courage runs out.

That's the Crusade's real foothold in this valley. A chapel, an ossuary, a reliquary, and a High Inquisitor with a documented fondness for confessions.

I want somebody to walk the nave. Not clear it - WALK it, and look at the doors at the far end, and tell me what's holding them shut, because something is and it isn't a bar.

I won't go. I've been scouting a long time and I know the difference between a risk and a queue, and I have seen what happens to scouts who go down that nave.

You've come back from everywhere else in this valley. Come back from this one too.

objectives.label: the far doors of the Scarlet Crypt

quests.accept_text: Down the nave, to the far doors. Look at what's holding them - then come back.
quests.turn_in_text:
Held from the inside. By something that wanted to be in there with what's in there.

[Verrick is quiet.]

Right. Then this stopped being a camp outside a crypt some time ago and nobody up the chain has noticed.

quests.title: The High Inquisitor
quests.description:
High Inquisitor Fairbanks. He's at the far end of the sanctum, behind a loop of candlelit corridors, and he does not leave it.

I'm not going to give you a clever plan because I haven't got one. What I've got is a count: he has broken more Forsaken than this valley currently holds. That isn't rhetoric, I've kept the tally off their own dispatches.

His initiates fill the corridors between. You'll not get a clean run at him.

And here's my axiom, which I've said to every scout I've sent anywhere: nobody who goes down there should expect to come back.

So far the exception is you. I'd rather it stayed that way, but I'd be lying if I said that was the deciding factor.
quests.accept_text: The sanctum's far end, past the candlelit corridors. His initiates fill them.
quests.turn_in_text:
[Verrick writes the tally out and then draws a line under it.]

That's closed.

I've carried that number in my head for a week and I'd started adding to it in my sleep. It's a number now. It's finished.

quests.title: The Sealed Vaults
quests.description:
Fairbanks is down and the crypt still isn't ours, which is the part nobody upstairs will want to hear.

Two vaults left, one either side.

West is the ossuary, under Valdric Bonewarden. That's where the Crusade put the dead they never finished burying - OUR dead, mostly, from this valley, stacked and catalogued and left in a condition I'd rather describe to you afterwards.

East is the reliquary, and that's Brother Wystan's. Whatever the Scarlets thought worth saving is in there, and given what they threw away, I would dearly love to know what met their standard.

Both. Open them both, and then this crypt belongs to the valley again.
quests.accept_text: Both vaults - the ossuary west under Valdric, the reliquary east under Wystan.
quests.turn_in_text:
[Verrick comes down off the rocks for the first time in a week.]

Both open. The whole crypt.

We'll get our dead out of that ossuary and put them in ground that belongs to them, and whatever's in the reliquary goes to Krell and then to the Undercity and becomes somebody else's problem.

You've cleared this valley end to end. Go and find Krell - he'll have worked out by now that he has nothing left to send you at.
